동생이 공부를 더 잘하니까 동생 학비라도 모으려고 바로 일을 구하는 중이었고, 내성적이고 외모 때문에 면접마다 떨어졌다고 함

3. 박명수가 직접 면접을 봄
얼굴 무섭고 말투 냉소적이라 쫄았는데, 알바하는 이유랑 수능 점수(400점 만점에 338점) 듣더니,
"내일부터 나와. 아니 오늘 시간 돼? 그냥 오늘부터 일해"

4. 둘째 날엔 2만원 주면서,
"너나 나같이 못생긴 애들은 깔끔하기라도 해야 해!"
머리 자르고 오라고 ㅋㅋㅋ

바쁠 땐 일부러 이 사람만 연장근무 시키고 택시비를 넉넉히 줬는데, 너무 많다고 하니까,
"내가 사장이야. 주는 대로 받아! 빨리 꺼져"

5. 첫 월급 봉투엔 30만원이 더 들어 있었음
박명수가 "장사도 안 되는데 더 준 거니까 감사해하고, 앞으로 충성을 다해 노예처럼 일해라" 하더니 "그 돈 쓰라고 주는 거 아니고 모았다가 대학 가라. 네 머리는 대학 가야 한다"

6. 그 결과, 그렇게 돈 모으고 수능 다시 봐서 본인도 동생도 대학 들어감
대학 다니면서도 저녁 알바 했는데 박명수가 근무시간을 맞춰줬고, 졸업하고 취업해서 지금은 결혼해서 애 둘 키운다고 함
연락처가 없어서 직접 인사는 못 했고, TV에 박명수 나오면 애들한테 "아빠 어릴 때 많이 도와주신 분"이라고 한다고🥹

7. 이게 처음도 아님
2010년 4월에도 포털 게시판에 대기업 들어간 남자 선배가 대학 때 박명수 도움 덕에 공부를 제때 마쳤다는 글이 올라옴
그 선배는 박명수 치킨집 배달 알바로 모은 등록금을 집안 사정 때문에 집에 보내고 복학을 미루려던 상황이었음

8. 그때 박명수가 150만원쯤 든 봉투를 주면서,
"공부는 때가 있는 법인데 미루지 마라. 성공해서 갚으라"

9. 취업하고 갚으러 갔더니,
"지금은 집에 보내드리고 나중에 더 잘되면 달라"
결국 안 받으심
그리고 2008년 박명수 결혼식장에서 돌려줬다고 ㅎㅎ
박명수가 "이제 받아도 될 것 같다. 넌 밥 두 그릇 먹고 가라" 했다는 얘기.

이형님 진심으로 댓가를 바라지 않고 선행을 베푸시는 형님임
롱런하는데는 다 이유가 있다는🫡

x.text:
🚨 Anthropic's $1.5 TRILLION IPO is already turning into a disaster.

Morgan Stanley has removed a major source of buying support for Anthropic's stock just ONE DAY after its historic IPO.

And the timing is absolutely insane.

Anthropic's shares surged above $111 on their debut before crashing nearly 28% from their peak.

But the bigger story is what Morgan Stanley just did.

• IPO stabilization: Morgan Stanley was appointed to help protect Anthropic's share price from heavy selling after its market debut.

• 147 MILLION shares: The bank had an option to buy additional shares directly from Anthropic at the $83 IPO price.

• Buying support: Instead of exercising that option, the bank could have bought shares in the open market to cover its short position, potentially supporting the stock during a crash.

• Option exhausted: Morgan Stanley exercised the entire 147 million-share option immediately, removing that potential source of buying support.

• $93.5 BILLION: The decision helped Anthropic raise a record amount of money through its IPO.

• Investors: With the stabilization option exhausted, shareholders no longer have that potential buying support if selling pressure continues.

And this is what makes the decision so controversial.

Underwriters typically have up to 30 days to exercise this option.

Morgan Stanley used the entire option after just ONE DAY, even as Anthropic shares were coming under serious pressure.

Market experts are already questioning the timing.

Anthropic walked away with $93.5 BILLION in IPO proceeds, while investors lost a potential source of support during one of the stock's most volatile periods.

For the biggest IPO in history, this is a brutal start.

And without that potential buying support, another major selloff could put even more pressure on the stock.

🚨 Elon Musk just warned that the AI industry could face a MASSIVE CASH CRISIS in 2027.

He says AI companies could need HUNDREDS OF BILLIONS in additional cash just to keep their massive data center projects running.

And the numbers behind his warning are absolutely insane.

• $1 TRILLION: Goldman Sachs estimates global AI investment could exceed this amount in 2026 alone.

• $1.2 TRILLION: Goldman projects spending by the five largest U.S. hyperscalers could reach this level in 2027.

• $1 TRILLION: Goldman also expects AI-related debt financing to reach this amount in 2027.

• Hundreds of billions: Musk warns that even a few months of delays could leave the industry needing this much extra cash.

Here's why this is such a serious problem.

Companies are spending enormous amounts of money on chips, servers, data centers and electricity before those investments generate revenue.

But getting all that computing power installed, cooled and running reliably takes time.

If projects get delayed by even a few months, companies still have to pay their bills while waiting for revenue to start coming in.

And when nearly $1 TRILLION is being spent every year, even small delays can create an enormous cash shortage.

Goldman has already warned that major AI hyperscalers collectively reported negative free cash flow in Q3 2026.

That means the industry is becoming increasingly dependent on borrowing and outside financing to keep expanding.

And if lenders become less willing to provide that money, some companies could be forced to delay projects, cut spending or raise even more expensive debt.

Musk's warning is not about AI demand disappearing.

It's about companies potentially running short of cash before their massive investments can start paying for themselves.

The AI industry could have trillions in spending commitments, enormous demand and still face a brutal funding crisis.

And Musk is already questioning where all that extra money will come from.

x.text:
In case anyone is curious:

We’ve had a ~pixel-perfect world model since last year, which is critical for synthetic data generation. 

The (much) smaller version of that in the car is a conditional mean-flow model, based on the recent sequence of Tesla Universal Vision Encoder features, which are the same ones that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions. 

We fork off from these UVE features, then run a separate ~1B diffusion model. This takes in the previous reality-view generation with added noise and then denoises it to the current visualization. 

It then produces a small video chunk (8 images at 36 fps, at the resolution of the UI screen). This work is done by 1/2 of a TRIP engine every UVE frame at 18 hz and is spread over 4 cycles. 

Currently, the latency is a bit high due to compute constraints, but we have ways to interleave newer UVE features along the diffusion transformer layers to cut roughly 35% of the latency.

"Trade for long enough, and you discover that the market has a godlike ability to peer into your soul, learn your character flaws, your private fears, weaknesses, pain thresholds. And the market uses this knowledge to tease you, sometimes letting you get away with recklessness, rewarding your greed, luring you to commit more brazen sins. At other times it creates false hope that you’ll escape whatever predicament you’ve gotten yourself into, allowing you to believe your own lies, letting you imagine you’ll slip its grasp this one time. Just like it did to leveraged Nvidia longs this Tuesday evening, when a blowout earnings report lifted the stock sharply higher after hours. By Friday's close it had lost 23% on the week. The process wears you down, so that at your weakest moment you puke positions at the absolute low, knowing it’s almost certainly a mistake, but grateful to end the torture. And breathe again.

When enough people hold the same view and pair it with arrogance, the market rounds up the herd and culls it in a violent flush. One man’s stop loss pushes price lower to the next man’s point of maximum pain, a runaway wildfire, a scorched earth cleanse. Sodom. Gomorrah. Like in February 2018, when the sellers of equity volatility watched their hallowed inverse VIX products lose 96% of their value in a ferocious afternoon. There was no specific catalyst. No real reason. Just the market gods at work. And it’s the very personal struggle with this omniscient superintelligence that makes those of us who have survived more introspective and humbler with time. It keeps us on the lookout for those moments when the herd has been rounded up and is being led to slaughter. Doing everything in our power to avoid that fate, and to capitalize on the chaos."

Eric Peters, One River Asset Management

THE AI CRASH IS ALREADY WORSE THAN THE DOT-COM CRASH FOR SOME OF TECH'S BIGGEST NAMES.

Out of 27 major tech stocks, 10 have already fallen more than they had at this point in 2000.

Nvidia is down 48% from its high this year, versus 32% at this point in 2000.

Intel, Oracle, Corning and Western Digital are all down around 60% or more.

The only reason the market doesn't look like 2000 yet is the mega caps.

Apple, Microsoft and Amazon are holding up, while back in 2000 they had already crashed 40% to 75% by this point.

The stocks holding up best are the ones that make most of their money outside AI, from iPhones, online shopping, Windows and Office.

The ones getting crushed are the companies whose growth depends on AI spending: chips, memory, data center fiber and AI cloud.

If AI spending keeps slowing, the pain could spread further.

x.text:
Even though Nehru died before the concept of the internet even existed, what is this obsession with crediting the Nehru-Gandhi family for "bringing" the internet, phones, and computers to India?

What does "brought" even mean here? Did they personally pack routers and microchips in their carry-on luggage on a flight back from Silicon Valley? These technologies were invented in the West and were bound to spread globally through basic market forces and human progress, unless the West restricted them or the recipient country itself rejected them. They reached every nation on Earth, from bustling economies to the most remote and backward contries.

India, being a bigger market, should have received technology earlier than smaller regional economies, but some of you will be shocked to know that even Pakistan received cellular service five years before India. So, if anything, this family's policies should be questioned for delaying the arrival of technology rather than credited for bringing it.

x.name: The Kobeissi Letter
x.text:
US net equity inflows are up to ~3.0% of GDP, their highest on record in data going back to the 1980s.

Net equity inflows measure foreign purchases of US stocks minus US investors' purchases of foreign equities.

This figure has risen nearly +5.0 percentage points since the 2022 bear market low.

Meanwhile, net debt inflows, which measure foreign purchases of US debt securities, such as Treasuries minus US purchases of foreign debt securities, are down to ~1.8%, their lowest since 2022.

As a result, net equity inflows have surpassed net debt inflows as a % of GDP by the widest margin since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

In other words, foreign investors are increasingly directing money towards US equities rather than US bonds.

Overseas demand for US equities has never been this strong.

Odia is my first language, English my second and Hindi my third, though I’m perfectly fluent in all three; I speak English with my friends from MP and UP just as I do with those from Andhra & Telangana, Karnataka, TN and Kerala. Hindi is a regional language in several northern states, no different in principle from Odia in Odisha, and neither should be presumed to be everyone’s default. In a country as linguistically diverse as India, English serves as the most practical lingua franca; my Hindi fluency, however, is particularly impressive when it comes to swear words.

Full Nvidia Press Release

NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board. The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead NVIDIA. In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead NVIDIA, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board. 

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as NVIDIA’s Chief Financial Officer.” Harvey Jones will remain as Board chair.

“I am honored to return to NVIDIA and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the NVIDIA Board for its confidence and deliberation through this process. I am especially grateful to Harvey Jones for his leadership as Chair, and to Colette Kress and our executive staff for leading NVIDIA during this period. I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support. Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.” 

As previously announced, in light of recent reporting that Mr. Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, the Board formed a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate, and the committee retained independent counsel to assist it in that investigation. The Board reiterated that the committee’s investigation will proceed to conclusion. Mr. Huang fully supports the investigation and is committed to cooperating with it.

The Board also recently formed a National Security and Export Control Committee comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks. The committee is engaging counsel with experience in national security matters, and such counsel will be retaining advisors with expertise in national security matters. NVIDIA is commencing a search to fill a new position, Chief Compliance Officer, to oversee compliance across NVIDIA and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee. NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries.

Meta’s chief AI officer, Alexandr Wang, says it’s hard to see how humanity keeps control of AI that can improve itself without limits.

“It is hard to imagine a world where humanity can maintain control over fully unconstrained recursive self-improvement,” Wang wrote in an essay titled “Superintelligence is Arriving.” “It is equally hard to imagine a world where humanity maintains control with superintelligence that is 1000x smarter and more capable than humans in every field.”

Wang pointed to this week’s machine-checked proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, one of math’s most famous unsolved problems, achieved “with the help of an alien mind that we don’t understand.” He said the industry must take “meaningfully different actions” from its current path to keep humans in control, but didn’t specify what those should be.

Strategic and ecosystem: As we had written previously, we believe Mr. Huang's vision, reach, and external convening power has been important to both Nvidia and the broader AI ecosystem. Leadership and culture: As we had written previously, we believe Mr. Huang has been integral to Nvidia's corporate culture and ethos - and we believe his return will largely reinforce the company's existing culture. We continue to expect the company to execute on its previously announced product roadmap.

Financial and regulatory: As previously reported in the press, the US Department of Justice has been conducting an investigation into whether some of Nvidia's customers did engage in export control violations following shipments of products to jurisdictions including Singapore. We continue to believe Nvidia's operations in certain jurisdictions could face more scrutiny going forward. In addition, press reports have also suggested that an SEC investigation into the company's past disclosures is underway. We believe these investigations are likely to serve as an overhang on the stock until they are resolved, and/or the company provides more disclosure on these items.

🚨 Was Nvidia's $1 TRILLION comeback the biggest stock market manipulation of 2026?

The sequence of events surrounding Jensen Huang's exit and return as Nvidia CEO is raising some very serious questions.

First, Huang faced allegations of possible spying links, with reports that senior U.S. officials wanted him removed.

Then Nvidia crashed nearly 50% from its peak, reaching its lowest level in over two years.

And just when investors thought things couldn't get worse, news of an SEC accounting investigation added even more panic before Friday's close.

But what happened over the weekend changed everything.

Scott Bessent changed his tone on Huang, and the same government that had raised concerns about him later supported his return.

Then came Monday's massive reversal.

Nvidia was already up 11% in pre-market trading, even though there had been no announcement about Huang's return.

Then the news broke that Jensen Huang was coming back as CEO, and Nvidia surged another 35%, adding nearly $1 TRILLION in market value and becoming the world's second most valuable company again.

Now think about what happened to ordinary investors.

They watched the CEO leave amid spying allegations, saw news of an SEC investigation, and sold as the stock collapsed.

Meanwhile, anyone who bought near the bottom could have made enormous gains in just a few days.

And the biggest question is why Nvidia was already up 11% before the news even came out.

Did some major investors know Huang was returning before everyone else?

If anyone used advance information to profit from this crash and recovery, this could become one of the biggest insider-trading scandals in recent history.

U.S. home prices rose 2.1% year-over-year in September, unchanged from August, according to the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller National Home Price Index.

The data highlight a widening gap between nominal home-price gains and inflation-adjusted housing returns.

The Trump administration is preparing to announce higher tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and more than a dozen other economies as soon as Tuesday, according to Bloomberg.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is expected to conclude the investigation under Section 301 of the 1974 Trade Act, which permits tariffs targeting unfair trade practices.

The announcement could mark a major escalation in global trade tensions.

The US equity market has recorded an average of 1 correction of 10%+ per year since 1930.

By comparison, a bear market has occurred once every 3.3 years on average over the same period.

Market corrections are a natural feature of equity markets.

An astronomer at the SETI Institute independently found the same signal and one other that Kevin had flagged. For the star in Lyra, astronomers now know when to watch for the next dip.

President Donald Trump told the New York Post he would consider granting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang a presidential pardon if necessary, although he doubts one will be needed.

“It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” Trump said.

Trump also urged Huang to testify truthfully before Congress next week, suggesting he would not need to invoke the Fifth Amendment.

Separately, Trump said a U.S. government equity stake in Nvidia remains a possibility, adding that it is “probably not too late.”

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) announced that there was an equipment outage at O’Hare International Airport in Chicago, Illinois, at 4.06 p.m. ET Tuesday. At 5 p.m. ET this was updated to a ground delay with an average wait of 47 minutes.

x.text:
🚨 THE UNITED STATES IS UNDER A MASSIVE CYBERATTACK

FinCEN, the agency responsible for tracking money laundering, suspicious banking transactions and terrorist financing, has confirmed unauthorized access to some of its systems.

And the breach is already affecting financial reporting across America.

Here's what happened:

• Systems shut down: FinCEN took some systems offline as a precaution while investigating the breach.

• Banking reports disrupted: Technical problems have prevented some financial institutions from meeting their reporting deadlines.

• Emergency extension: Certain reporting deadlines have been pushed to December 30.

• Sensitive financial data: FinCEN receives reports containing information about suspicious transactions, businesses and individuals. Authorities have not confirmed whether any of this information was stolen.

And this comes after a disturbing series of incidents across major institutions.

Over the past two weeks:

• Microsoft 365 suffered a major outage.
• The FAA grounded flights nationwide.
• Major U.S. banks and airlines experienced service disruptions.
• Charles Schwab and Apple reported outages.
• Equinor disclosed a cyberattack.
• The CIA suffered a separate breach involving unclassified intelligence systems.

And now the U.S. Treasury's financial crime reporting operations have been disrupted by a confirmed cybersecurity incident.

The biggest unanswered question is whether hackers accessed the sensitive financial intelligence that banks submit to FinCEN.

Authorities have not identified the attackers, confirmed what information was compromised or established any connection between these incidents.

🚨 The current AI market crash looks TERRIFYINGLY similar to the 2000 dot-com crash

On March 10, 2000, the Nasdaq peaked. 

Just 48 days later, AT&T Wireless raised $10.6 BILLION in what was then the biggest IPO in U.S. history.

26 years later, the Nasdaq peaked on October 6, 2026.

And just 44 days later, Anthropic completed the biggest IPO in history, raising $93.5 BILLION.

But the timing of these record breaking IPOs is only the beginning.

Look at what else is happening:

• Massive infrastructure spending: In 2000, companies poured billions into telecom networks. Today, it's AI data centers. 

Annual AI investment is projected to exceed 3% of U.S. GDP, compared with just 1.1% during the internet boom.

• Aggressive monetary tightening: The Fed raised rates six times from 4.75% to 6.5% between 1999 and 2000. 

Today, markets are once again dealing with tighter monetary policy while technology stocks struggle.

• Credit market stress: Financing became increasingly difficult for tech companies during the dot-com crash. 

Today, credit risk is rising across major AI companies, with bond investors expecting Anthropic's debt to receive a junk rating.

• Extreme valuations: Unprofitable internet companies attracted billions in 2000. 

Today, Anthropic has reached a fully diluted valuation above $2 TRILLION despite reporting a $104 BILLION net loss in the first nine months of 2026.

And the amount of money involved today is MUCH bigger.

Major U.S. technology companies are projected to spend $5.5 TRILLION by 2030, even as borrowing costs rise and investors question whether AI can generate enough profits to justify the spending.

Remember what happened in 2000.

The internet went on to change the entire world, but that didn't stop the Nasdaq from crashing 77%.

It took roughly 15 YEARS for the index to recover its previous all-time high.

AI could transform the global economy just like the internet did.

But even if AI becomes the biggest technological revolution in history, investors could still lose TRILLIONS along the way.

🚨 This isn't a good sign for the US bond market.

The U.S. Treasury just sold $44 Billion in 7Y bonds, but investors demanded higher interest rates than expected.

The bonds were sold at a yield of 4.708%, compared to the 4.698% expected before the auction.

This means the government had to offer higher returns to attract buyers.

And the numbers show why.

Investors placed $2.43 in bids for every $1 of bonds offered, while major bond dealers ended up buying just 8.61% of the total.

So demand wasn't terrible, but it was weaker than the market expected.

What's concerning is that Treasury yields had already fallen roughly 10 basis points earlier in the day as investors bought US bonds.

Yet when another $44 Billion in government debt came up for sale, buyers still wanted a slightly better deal.

And this is happening while the US continues borrowing heavily and inflation remains well above the Fed's 2% target.

If investors keep demanding higher returns to buy government debt, borrowing could become more expensive for the US.

One weak auction won't trigger a crisis, but repeated weak auctions could put even more pressure on America's already massive debt burden.

🚨 The Fed's next rate hike could be its last.

US PCE inflation just hit a 5-month high of 3.8%, while core PCE climbed to 3.3%.

Both are still well above the Fed's 2% target, but inflation is starting to slow on a monthly basis:

• PCE: 0.5% → 0.3%
• CPI: 0.6% → 0.4%
• PPI: 1.4% → 0.3%

Another important thing to keep in mind is that these are October's numbers.

Since the US midterm elections, WTI crude oil has fallen roughly 14%..

Rising energy prices were one of the biggest reasons inflation picked up over the past few months. 

Now that oil prices are falling, we could see some relief in November's inflation data.

The market still expects the Fed to raise rates by 25 bps on December 9.

But before its next meeting in January, the Fed will have three new inflation reports:

• December 10: CPI
• December 15: PPI
• December 23: PCE

If inflation starts coming down, it will become much harder for the Fed to justify more aggressive rate hikes.

Mortgage rates are already above 7%, the housing market is struggling, and stocks are under heavy selling pressure.

The last thing the US economy needs right now is another round of aggressive rate hikes.

Unless energy prices start rising again, December's rate hike could be the last of this cycle.

Gold has rarely been this oversold:

Gold prices are trading -20% below their 200-day moving average, their largest negative deviation since June 2013.

This marks a sharp reversal from the +45% deviation above the 200-day moving average recorded in January, the largest since the 1970s.

This comes as gold prices have dropped -37% from their January intraday peak, their largest drawdown within a 12-month period since the early 1980s.

By comparison, during the 2008 Financial Crisis, gold prices also declined -20% below their 200-day moving average.

However, the largest such negative deviation was recorded in 1981, at -27%.

Gold is experiencing one of its most severe declines in history.

x.name: Nick Timiraos
x.text:
How would the Warsh Fed address market signals saying financial conditions are tightening, with an inflation picture that still looks uncomfortably hot? I wrote about the issue here: https://t.co/E5dwVHFA53  Despite some easy parallels to the December 2018 situation the Powell Fed faced (A new chair! Trump facing a midterm setback! A hawkish committee! Risk-off!), the inflation backdrop is so different that the comparison struggles to reveal much.

Consider: At that December meeting, the committee's leading intellectual dove, Jim Bullard of the St. Louis Fed, warned colleagues that raising rates risked looking "tone deaf." He presciently predicted that the yield curve would invert if they kept going. But he added a caveat that looks very different today: 

"Taking these types of risks at a meeting like this might be worth it if inflation was running above target and we really felt that we had to be aggressive to keep inflation and inflation expectations contained. But it's not running above target."

x.name: Nick Timiraos
x.text:
Before he became Fed chairman, Kevin Warsh spoke about the value of market signals and the risks of reacting too much to investors' whims. His view, in essence, is that the Fed should treat markets as valuable sources of information, not as something to protect. Watch them closely so as not to be caught flat-footed. But don't let falling prices push it into rescuing investors.

The trouble is that in real time, heeding a market signal and providing a put can look a lot alike. His comments are consistent in principle but hard to apply in practice. In December 2018, at a drawdown much like this month's, he came down on the side of pausing. 

• In a March 2016 speech, he faulted the Fed for "a systematic under-appreciation of contemporaneous market price signals, typically followed by a belated and panicky policy response that validates market assumptions of a central bank put." https://t.co/OXv6b4KZfX

• In October 2018, on Jim Grant's podcast, he presciently noted how rising 10-year Treasury yields (which were up 20 bps that week) would hit risk assets, but he didn't sound concerned: "I'm waiting for some commentator to call this another tantrum with yields moving up so swiftly. I would call it something else. I'd call it nature, gravity." He went on to explain his view that "10-year treasury yields should be equal to nominal GDP."

"The Federal Reserve and other forecasters now appear to have been mugged by the recent data. So real economy's growing at 3.5%. Inflation, at least as measured by the government, is growing at 2%. So history and theory would say 10-year yields should be five and a half or so. So I'm not that overwhelmed by a 20 basis point move this week, but I think nature takes it in that direction."  Whether the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points in December "doesn't matter much in my view. The real job is to think hard about tail risks ... and upside risks."
He referred to the episode in early 2016, when an 11% stock drop led the Fed to defer rate hikes: "We'll need to watch the central bank and see how responsive they are to what I would say natural movements in asset prices… I hope that the focus is on the real side of the real economy rather than worried about what happens if the stock market falls 10% or bond yields move up 50 or 75 basis points. That ought not be their focus." https://t.co/vkYZgiloDi

• Most memorably, in December 2018, ten weeks later, in a WSJ op-ed with Stan Druckenmiller, with stocks down ~11%: Market indicators "aren't foolproof, but they have a better track record than economists," and the Fed "should cease—for now—its double-barreled blitz of higher interest rates and tighter liquidity." https://t.co/Q1FynnIlzz

x.text:
🚨 SoftBank's AI gamble is turning into its WORST STOCK MARKET CRASH since 2008.

SoftBank shares crashed another 14.8% on November 25, with over $200 BILLION in market value wiped out since June.

Here's how much SoftBank has fallen during major market crashes:

• Dot-com bubble (2000–02): -98.75%
• Financial crisis (2007–08): -80.06%
• COVID selloff (2019–20): -56.84%
• Tech selloff (2021–22): -60.63%
• AI selloff (2026): -70.77%

And its financial situation is becoming more worrying:

• Over $50 billion in new debt in just 12 months.
• $64.6 billion invested in OpenAI.
• $7 billion loss in its latest quarter.

SoftBank's entire company is now worth less on the stock market than the $99.6 billion value it reported for its OpenAI stake in September.

OpenAI is still a private company, and that valuation is based on SoftBank's own estimates.

If private AI companies start losing value, SoftBank may have to sell its holdings and cut funding for new projects to manage its growing debt.

This could create serious problems for the entire AI industry.

Less funding could mean fewer data centers, lower chip demand and falling revenues for companies supplying power and equipment.

A slowdown in AI spending could also trigger another massive selloff in global stock markets, where trillions of dollars in valuations depend on future AI growth.

It took SoftBank 21 years to recover from the dot-com crash.

The internet changed the world, but that didn't stop technology stocks from collapsing.

The same could happen with AI.

x.name: The Macro Paper
x.text:
🚨 AI DEBT CRISIS IS GETTING WORSE.

Wall Street is becoming increasingly worried about the massive debt behind the AI boom.

The cost of insuring debt from Oracle, SpaceX, Alphabet and CoreWeave against default has reportedly hit RECORD HIGHS.

Even Nvidia's massive stock rally following Jensen Huang's return failed to calm the AI debt market.

And the numbers are getting concerning.

• CoreWeave's estimated 5-year default probability reached 68%, based on credit market pricing.

• SoftBank's debt insurance costs reached 501 basis points, their highest level since October 2022.

• Oracle, Alphabet and SpaceX have also seen record levels in their debt insurance costs.

But Anthropic could be facing an even bigger problem.

Just days after its record breaking IPO, bond investors expect Anthropic's debt to receive a JUNK credit rating, according to WSJ.

The company has committed to spending roughly $900 BILLION on AI computing power over the coming years.

Despite generating $17 BILLION in revenue last quarter, Anthropic is still losing money because of its enormous computing costs.

It had $96 BILLION in cash before the IPO, but its future spending commitments are nearly 10 times that amount.

A junk rating would make borrowing more expensive and could limit its access to the $8.6 TRILLION investment-grade bond market.

And Anthropic isn't alone.

Nvidia and Broadcom have already guaranteed tens of billions of dollars in loans tied to AI chip purchases.

Meanwhile, major banks are trying to sell billions in data center loans as concerns about construction delays and financing risks continue to grow.

The problem is that AI companies still need hundreds of billions of dollars to complete their expansion plans.

But the lenders financing those projects are becoming more worried about whether they'll get their money back.

If borrowing costs continue rising, companies could be forced to delay projects, cut spending or seek more expensive financing.

And that could hit everyone from AI developers to chipmakers and data center operators.

The AI boom needs massive amounts of money to keep growing, but the debt market is already showing signs of trouble.

Less than a year after 26/11, Manmohan Singh told Parliament that dialogue and engagement with Pakistan were the best way forward when questioned about accountability for the attacks.

Shortly before this, he had met Pakistan’s PM in Egypt and delinked action on terrorism from the composite dialogue process, marking a shift from India’s post-26/11 stance that talks would resume only after Pakistan dismantled terror infrastructure and brought the perpetrators to justice.

In the same meeting, in a joint statement, both PMs described terrorism as a common threat to both nations, departing from India’s usual position of identifying Pakistan as the exporter of terrorism to India.

For the families of 26/11 victims, this was nothing short of an injustice. There was no meaningful accountability beyond sending dossiers, while Pakistan faced no consequences and showed little regard for India's demands. Instead of holding talks until the perpetrators were brought to justice and terror infrastructure dismantled, India resumed engagement with the very country from which the attacks were orchestrated.

🚨 The UK is repeating the mistakes that led to America's 2008 housing crisis.

Nationwide, one of Britain's largest mortgage lenders, has launched a new mortgage scheme with alarming borrowing limits:

• Just 1% deposit required.
• Borrow up to 99% of the property's value.
• Borrow up to 6 times your annual income if eligible.
• Loans of up to £750,000 for 40 years.

Before the 2008 crisis, US lenders were also lowering deposit requirements and making it easier for households to take on massive amounts of debt.

Everything looked fine until house prices started falling. Mortgage defaults surged, financial institutions collapsed, and the world entered a global recession.

While Nationwide still conducts affordability checks, a borrower with a 1% deposit could lose their entire initial equity with just a 1% decline in house prices.

A 10% housing crash could leave someone who bought a £500,000 home owing £45,000 more than their property is worth before repayments.

Instead of making homes more affordable, lenders are making it easier for households to take on more debt.

Is South Korea preparing for a massive stock market crisis?

The number of emergency measures announced by Korean authorities in recent weeks is becoming increasingly concerning.

• Nov 9: Suspended the mandatory 140% collateral requirement on margin loans to curb forced selling.

• Nov 22: Held an emergency meeting to discuss market stabilization measures.

• Nov 23: Put an $8 billion rescue fund on standby and contacted 25 financial institutions for additional funding.

• Nov 24: Relaxed share buyback restrictions and intensified monitoring of illegal short selling.

• Nov 25-26: Plans to expand the emergency rescue fund emerged.

The KOSPI has lost nearly 50% from its June peak, while the existing rescue fund represents just 0.3% of its market value.

The last time South Korea deployed such a rescue fund was during the 2008 global financial crisis.

Now, authorities are looking to increase its size before even deploying it.

If the global AI selloff continues, South Korea's stock market crisis could quickly turn into a much bigger economic crisis.

x.text:
IMAGINE EXPLAINING 1976 TO SOMEONE BORN IN 2026

For someone born today it's almost impossible to imagine just how different India was in 1976. The world has changed so much that things considered extraordinary back then are now part of our daily routine. We have new cities, bigger communities, more opportunities and a population that has crossed 140 crore. The number of districts has also grown from 356 to 780.

But there's one statistic that hasn't moved with the times. The Lok Sabha still has 543 seats. That means the institution representing the people of India has retained the same strength even as the number of people it represents has grown dramatically.

This is the larger conversation we need to have. Democracy isn't supposed to be frozen in time. It must evolve alongside the people it serves. India in 2026 is not India in 1976 and its Parliament should reflect that reality.

x.text:
🚨 US HOUSING MARKET IS IN TROUBLE.

Housing makes up nearly 16% of the US economy, and homebuilders are already being forced to slash prices to attract buyers.

• Median new home prices have dropped 15% from their 2022 peak.

• Average new home prices plunged 12.1% YoY in October.

• 46% of builders are cutting prices, while 68% are offering incentives just to sell homes.

And builders are getting squeezed from both sides.

They're selling homes for less while construction and borrowing costs remain high.

Residential investment has already fallen in 6 of the last 8 quarters.

If this continues, builders could start cancelling projects, cutting construction, and laying off workers.

That would hit construction jobs, suppliers, and businesses that depend on new home sales.

A housing slowdown is already underway, and the damage could spread across the US economy.

x.name: The Macro Paper
x.text:
🚨 The bond market is warning the Fed to stop.

The US 2Y yield is getting closer to crossing above the 5Y yield.

Historically, yield curve inversions have often resulted in weaker economic growth, which forces the Fed to lower interest rates.

This is another reason why December could be the Fed's last rate hike.

Falling oil and commodity prices are already easing inflationary pressures, while the bond market is signaling concerns about economic growth.

If the Fed continues raising rates, higher borrowing costs could further weaken consumer spending, business investment, and employment.

The longer the Fed keeps monetary policy restrictive, the greater the risk of pushing the US economy into a recession.

The Fed may soon have to shift its focus from fighting inflation to preventing a recession.

This is also its 2nd-highest reading since the 2022 bear market, when it peaked at 4.0%.

On Wednesday alone, this figure rose to 4.2%, while on last Friday it surged to 5.7%, its widest single-session intraday trading range since April 9th, 2025.

By comparison, during the 2020 pandemic and the 2008 Financial Crisis, the Nasdaq 100 saw 5-day average intraday ranges as much as 7.7% and 8.9%, respectively.

The largest 5-day average intraday range in the Nasdaq 100 was recorded following the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble burst, at 10.2% in January 2001.

Volatility across tech stocks is historically high.

Inflationary is intensifying in Japan:

Japan’s Services Producer Price Index (SPPI) jumped +4.2% YoY in October, its largest annual increase since 1990, and far above expectations of +3.6%.

This index tracks domestic prices businesses charge each other for services, and serves as a key inflation metric in Japan.

MoM, the index rose +1.1%, up from +0.3% in the previous month and marking its biggest monthly increase in 6 months.

The latest surge was driven particularly by higher ocean freight transportation costs, leasing costs, and hotel charges.

Prices in transport and postal activities alone jumped +9.4% YoY in October, following an +8.4% increase in September.

Rising inflationary pressures are strengthening the case for a December rate hike by the Bank of Japan.
